title: Taiwan President Urges Micron to Avert Strike at Primary HBM Hub
summary:
A new packaging plant in central Taiwan opened recently as Micron management and labor unions clashed over employee bonus schemes. President William Lai has since urged both parties to negotiate "sincerely" to avoid a strike that would disrupt the supply of high bandwidth memory (HBM) chips. One labor union claims it already possesses sufficient votes to initiate a walkout during a period of severe global memory chip shortages.

Taiwan is Micron's largest manufacturing base, employing 15,000 people and serving as the company's primary center for HBM chip production. Over the last 30 years, Micron has invested $45 billion, or NT$1.4 trillion, in the region. The packaging facility attended by Lai was constructed and made operational in slightly over one year.
